# Identifying Important Predictors of Bioavailability

To determine the relative importance of each BLM predictor on trace element bioavailability, we will conduct a multiple linear regressions (MLR), use step wise selection of the most important predictors, and determine their standardized beta coefficients using the formula:

total bioavailable element = sum of BLM predictors (as standardized log-transformed variables)

## 1. Assess correlation

```{r}
# Spearman correlation matrix of all BLM predictors
BLM_predict <- c("log_Zn_nM", "log_Cu_nM", "log_Temp_C", 
                    "pH", "log_DOC_nM", "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM", 
                    "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM", 
                    "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM")

library(dplyr)

cor_df_std <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(BLM_predict)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), scale)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

cor_mat <- cor(
  cor_df_std,
  method = "spearman",
  use    = "pairwise.complete.obs"
)

# Plot & save
library(corrplot)

out_dir <- "Multiple linear regression"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

png(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Spearman_correlation_BLM_predictors.png"),
  width    = 2400,
  height   = 2000,
  res      = 300
)

corrplot(
  cor_mat,
  method      = "color",
  type        = "upper",
  order       = "hclust",
  tl.col      = "black",
  tl.cex      = 0.8,
  addCoef.col = "black",
  number.cex  = 0.7,
  diag        = FALSE
)

dev.off()

```

## 2. Build MLR

Use log-transformed and standardized variables to build a large model, calculate standardized beta coefficients, variance inflation factors (VIF), and relative importance on bioavailability

```{r}
library(MASS)
library(car)
library(relaimpo)
library(dplyr)
library(openxlsx)
library(corrplot)

vars_to_select <- c("log_Zn_nM", "log_Temp_C", 
                    "pH", "log_DOC_nM", "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM", 
                    "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM", 
                    "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM")

# 0. Standardize variables
std_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g, all_of(vars_to_select)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ as.numeric(scale(.x)), .names = "{.col}_std")) %>%
  dplyr::select(ends_with("_std")) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Define the standardized predictor names + standardized response
vars_to_select_std <- paste0(vars_to_select, "_std")
response_std <- "log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g_std"

# Model formula using standardized columns
form_std <- reformulate(vars_to_select_std, response = response_std)

# 1. Full MLR
full_mod <- lm(form_std, data = std_vars)
full_mod_summary <- summary(full_mod)

# 2. Estimates (standardized partial slopes) + p-values
coef_table <- full_mod_summary$coefficients

est_df <- data.frame(
  Predictor = rownames(coef_table),
  Estimate  = coef_table[, "Estimate"],
  p_value   = coef_table[, "Pr(>|t|)"]
) %>%
  filter(Predictor != "(Intercept)")

# 3. VIF
vif_vals <- vif(full_mod)

vif_df <- data.frame(
  Predictor = names(vif_vals),
  VIF       = as.numeric(vif_vals)
)

# 4. Relative importance (lmg)
rel_imp <- calc.relimp(full_mod, type = "lmg", rela = TRUE)

rel_df <- data.frame(
  Predictor = names(rel_imp$lmg),
  Rel_Importance = as.numeric(rel_imp$lmg)
)

# 5. Combine summary table
final_table <- est_df %>%
  left_join(vif_df, by = "Predictor") %>%
  left_join(rel_df, by = "Predictor") %>%
  arrange(desc(Rel_Importance))

final_table

# 6. Create full coefficient table for separate Excel sheet
coef_tab <- as.data.frame(full_mod_summary$coefficients)
coef_tab$Predictor <- rownames(coef_tab)
coef_tab <- coef_tab %>%
  relocate(Predictor)

# 7. Create model summary table for separate Excel sheet
model_stats <- data.frame(
  Metric = c(
    "Residual standard error",
    "R-squared",
    "Adjusted R-squared",
    "F-statistic",
    "Numerator df",
    "Denominator df"
  ),
  Value = c(
    full_mod_summary$sigma,
    full_mod_summary$r.squared,
    full_mod_summary$adj.r.squared,
    unname(full_mod_summary$fstatistic["value"]),
    unname(full_mod_summary$fstatistic["numdf"]),
    unname(full_mod_summary$fstatistic["dendf"])
  )
)

# 8. Save workbook
out_dir <- "Multiple linear regression"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

write.xlsx(
  list(
    Final_Table = final_table,
    Full_Model_Coefficients = coef_tab,
    Full_Model_Summary = model_stats
  ),
  file = file.path(out_dir, "MLR.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

## 3. Partial slope plots

Partial regression plots of log BLM parameters

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)

# 1. Extract retained predictors from stepwise model
retained_vars <- names(coef(full_mod))[-1]  # drop intercept

# 2. Function to get partial residuals for each predictor
get_partial_df <- function(model, data, var) {
  # Construct model formula terms
  all_terms <- attr(terms(model), "term.labels")
  other_terms <- setdiff(all_terms, var)
  
  # Get residuals of Y on all predictors except the variable of interest
  y_formula <- reformulate(other_terms, response = all.vars(formula(model))[1])
  y_resid <- resid(lm(y_formula, data = data))
  
  # Get residuals of X_var on all other predictors
  x_formula <- reformulate(other_terms, response = var)
  x_resid <- resid(lm(x_formula, data = data))
  
  df <- data.frame(
    predictor = x_resid,
    response = y_resid,
    variable = var
  )
  return(df)
}

# 3. Build combined dataset for all retained predictors
partial_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(retained_vars, get_partial_df, 
                                    model = full_mod, data = std_vars))

# 4. Plot partial regression slopes
step.mod_partial_slopes <-
  ggplot(partial_df, aes(x = predictor, y = response)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue") + #95% CI
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    x = "Predictor (residuals)",
    y = "Response (residuals)",
    title = "Standardized Partial Regression Plots of Predictors"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

step.mod_partial_slopes

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Partial_slopes_MLR.png"),
  plot     = step.mod_partial_slopes,
  width    = 8,
  height   = 6,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

## 4. Outlier detection

```{r}
# 1. Get model diagnostics
model_diag <- influence.measures(full_mod)

# 2. Extract indices of influential points flagged by diagnostics
infl_points <- which(apply(model_diag$is.inf, 1, any))

# 3. Create a dataframe with their info
flagged_obs <- data.frame(
  Sample_ID = dat$Sample_ID[infl_points],
  Fitted = fitted(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Residual = residuals(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Std_Residual = rstandard(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Leverage = hatvalues(full_mod)[infl_points],
  Cooks_D = cooks.distance(full_mod)[infl_points])

# View flagged observations
flagged_obs

# Save
library(openxlsx)

write.xlsx(
  flagged_obs,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "MLR_flagged_obs.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

Determine whether these flagged observations are clustered around a certain characteristic

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# 1. Add descriptive variables from dat to flagged observations (already done)
flagged_obs <- flagged_obs %>%
  left_join(dat %>% 
              dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Site, Date, Typology, Development), 
            by = "Sample_ID")

### ---- By Typology ----
# 2a. Summarize how many flagged points per cluster
by_typ <- flagged_obs %>% count(Typology)

# 2b. Proportion of flagged by cluster
prop_typ <- flagged_obs %>%
  count(Typology) %>%
  mutate(prop_flagged = n / sum(n))

# 2c. Overall proportions in dataset
overall_typ <- dat %>%
  count(Typology) %>%
  mutate(prop_overall = n / sum(n))

# 2d. Compare flagged vs overall
compare_typ <- left_join(prop_typ, overall_typ, by = "Typology")


### ---- By Site ----
# 3a. Summarize flagged points per site
by_site <- flagged_obs %>% count(Site)

# 3b. Proportion flagged per site
prop_site <- flagged_obs %>%
  count(Site) %>%
  mutate(prop_flagged = n / sum(n))

# 3c. Overall proportions in dataset
overall_site <- dat %>%
  count(Site) %>%
  mutate(prop_overall = n / sum(n))

# 3d. Compare flagged vs overall
compare_site <- left_join(prop_site, overall_site, by = "Site")

### ---- By Developed LULC ----
# 4a. Summarize flagged points per site
by_dev <- flagged_obs %>% count(Development)

# 4b. Proportion flagged per site
prop_dev <- flagged_obs %>%
  count(Development) %>%
  mutate(prop_flagged = n / sum(n))

# 4c. Overall proportions in dataset
overall_dev <- dat %>%
  count(Development) %>%
  mutate(prop_overall = n / sum(n))

# 4d. Compare flagged vs overall
compare_dev <- left_join(prop_dev, overall_dev, by = "Development")


# 5. Combine plots
library(dplyr)

compare_typ <- compare_typ %>% 
  rename(Value = Typology)

compare_site <- compare_site %>% 
  rename(Value = Site)

compare_dev <- compare_dev %>% 
  rename(Value = Development) 

# 6. Now combine all tables
flagged_obs_clusters <- bind_rows(compare_typ, compare_site, compare_dev)

# 7. Check result
flagged_obs_clusters

# 8. Save
library(openxlsx)

# Path to file
file_path <- file.path(out_dir, "MLR_flagged_obs.xlsx")

# Load existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook(file_path)

# Add new worksheet
addWorksheet(wb, "Flagged_Obs_Clusters")

# Write data to the new sheet
writeData(
  wb,
  sheet = "Flagged_Obs_Clusters",
  x = flagged_obs_clusters
)

# Save workbook (overwrite = TRUE updates the file)
saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
```

## 1. Summary Statistics

Mean and standard error by typology

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Standard error function
se <- function(x) {
  sd(x, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(x)))
}

# Mode function (returns the most frequent value)
get_mode <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(NA)
  ux <- unique(x)
  ux[which.max(tabulate(match(x, ux)))]
}

summary_table <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, where(is.numeric)) %>%  
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Typology,
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean     = mean(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median   = median(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mode     = get_mode(Value),
    Variance = var(Value, na.rm = TRUE),
    SE       = se(Value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

summary_table
```

Export to excel

```{r}

file_path <- "Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx"

wb <- createWorkbook()
addWorksheet(wb, "Summary Stats")
writeData(wb, "Summary Stats", summary_table)
saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
```

## 2. Check of ANOVA Assumptions

### a. Normality

By Shapiro-Wilk

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(writexl)

# Set alpha for normality
alpha <- 0.05

# Identify numeric variables (same as before)
numeric_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

# Initialize results dataframe
shapiro_results <- data.frame(
  Variable = character(),
  W_statistic = numeric(),
  p_value = numeric(),
  Normal = logical(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop over variables
for (var in numeric_vars) {
  
  # Remove NA values (required for Shapiro test)
  x <- dat[[var]]
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  
  # Shapiro test only works for 3 <= n <= 5000
  if (length(x) >= 3 && length(x) <= 5000) {
    
    test <- shapiro.test(x)
    
    W_val <- test$statistic
    p_val <- test$p.value
    
    normal <- p_val > alpha
    
  } else {
    # If sample size invalid, return NA
    W_val <- NA
    p_val <- NA
    normal <- NA
  }
  
  # Append results
  shapiro_results <- rbind(
    shapiro_results,
    data.frame(
      Variable = var,
      W_statistic = W_val,
      p_value = p_val,
      Normal = normal
    )
  )
}

# View results
shapiro_results

# Save
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist
if(!"Normality by Shapiro Wilk" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "Normality by Shapiro Wilk")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "Normality by Shapiro Wilk", shapiro_results)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

### b. Homogeneity of Variance

Using the Levene Test

```{r}
library(car)  # for leveneTest()
library(dplyr)

# Set alpha for homogeneity check
alpha <- 0.05

# Identify all numeric variables EXCEPT Typology
numeric_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

# Initialize results dataframe
levene_results <- data.frame(
  Variable = character(),
  F_value = numeric(),
  p_value = numeric(),
  Homogeneous = logical(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop over all numeric variables
for (var in numeric_vars) {
  
  # Run Levene's test
  test <- car::leveneTest(as.formula(paste(var, "~ Typology")), data = dat)
  
  # Extract F and p-values
  F_val <- test[1, "F value"]
  p_val <- test[1, "Pr(>F)"]
  
  # Determine homogeneity
  homogeneous <- p_val > alpha
  
  # Add results to dataframe
  levene_results <- rbind(
    levene_results, 
    data.frame(
      Variable = var,
      F_value = F_val,
      p_value = p_val,
      Homogeneous = homogeneous
    )
  )
}

# View results
levene_results

# Save
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist
if(!"Homog Var by Typology" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "Homog Var by Typology")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "Homog Var by Typology", levene_results)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

## 3. Kruskal Wallis Test

Since most variables fail the assumptions for an ANOVA, we will use a non-parametric rank-based test to determine whether variables significantly differ by stream typology; the Kruskal Wallis (KW) test. We will also use the Holm-Bonferroni correction factor for multiple comparisons when conducting pairwise comparisons of variables by typology.

KW test relies on the following assumptions

1.  ***For ordinal, interval, or ratio data:*** While most of our variables fail this assumption, we can make an exception while being aware of this.

2.  ***The samples are independent of each other and within each group:*** Our variables meet this assumption.

3.  ***The distributions of the groups should have the same shape.***

### a. Distribution of variables by typology

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Choose variables whose distributions you want to compare by Typology
blm_predictors <- c(
  "log_Zn_uM",
  "log_Temp_C", 
  "pH", 
  "log_DOC_uM",
  "log_DIC_uM", 
  "log_Cl_uM", 
  "log_Ca_uM",
  "log_Mg_uM", 
  "log_SO4_uM", 
  "log_Na_uM",
  "log_K_uM"
)

# Change to long format
dat_long <- dat %>%
  # Keep Typology and the variables you want to check
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(blm_predictors)) %>%
  
  # Turn columns into rows: Variable, Value
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

# Density plots by Typology
ggplot(dat_long, aes(x = Value, fill = Typology)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +   # alpha for transparent fill
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free") +  # one panel per Variable
  labs(
    title = "Distributions by Typology",
    x = "Value",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )
```

### b. Check for missing values

The KW test also can't handle variables with missing values and no variance, we'll check to see if any variables have these two conditions

```{r}
library(dplyr)

na_counts <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~sum(is.na(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "NA_count") %>%
  filter(NA_count > 0)

# View results, should be 0
na_counts

dat$log_Upstream_from_main_stem_km <- NULL
```

### c. Check for zero variance

No variables have missing values, now we'll check for lack of variance

```{r}
no_variance <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~dplyr::n_distinct(., na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "Variable",
               values_to = "Distinct_values") %>%
  filter(Distinct_values <= 1)

# View results, should be 0
no_variance
```

### d. Run KW tests

Now we can perform the KW test

```{r}
library(tibble)
library(agricolae)
library(dplyr)

alpha <- 0.05

# 1. Get all numeric variables in dat
numeric_vars <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(where(is.numeric)) %>%
  names()

# 2. Create an empty list to store rows
combined_list <- list()

# 3. Loop through each numeric variable 
i <- 1
for (v in numeric_vars) {
  
  # Kruskal-Wallis test
  formula <- as.formula(paste(v, "~ Typology"))
  kw_test <- kruskal.test(formula, data = dat)
  
  chi_sq     <- kw_test$statistic
  df_val     <- kw_test$parameter
  p_val      <- kw_test$p.value
  significant <- p_val < alpha   # significant when p < 0.05
  
  # agricolae::kruskal to assign groups (letters)
  k_out <- agricolae::kruskal(
    y    = dat[[v]],
    trt  = dat$Typology,
    alpha = alpha,
    group = TRUE
  )
  
  # Create a data frame from the groups table
  groups_df <- k_out$groups %>%
    rownames_to_column("Typology")
  
  # Combine test results with group letters
  combined_list[[i]] <- groups_df %>%
    mutate(
      Variable   = v,
      Chi_sq     = as.numeric(chi_sq),
      df         = as.numeric(df_val),
      p_value    = as.numeric(p_val),
      Significant = significant
    )
  
  i <- i + 1
}

# 5. Bind everything together
combined_kruskal <- bind_rows(combined_list)

# View
str(combined_kruskal)

# Save
library(openxlsx)

# Load the existing workbook
wb <- loadWorkbook("Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx")

# Create sheet if it does NOT exist
if(!"K-W test by Typology" %in% names(wb)) {
  addWorksheet(wb, "K-W test by Typology")
}

# Write your new table
writeData(wb, "K-W test by Typology", combined_kruskal)

# Save the workbook (overwrite)
saveWorkbook(wb, "Statistical_analyses_by_typology.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# 1. Titles for each variable's plot (panel title)
title_lookup <- c(
  "pH"         = "pH",
  "log_DOC_uM" = "Dissolved Organic Carbon",
  "log_DIC_uM" = "Dissolved Inorganic Carbon",
  "log_Ca_uM"  = "Calcium",
  "log_Mg_uM"  = "Magnesium",
  "log_Na_uM"  = "Sodium",
  "log_K_uM"   = "Potassium",
  "log_SO4_uM" = "Sulfate",
  "log_Cl_uM"  = "Chloride"
)


# 2. Make sure output folder exists
out_dir <- "Plots by typology"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# 2. Long format (DO NOT re-factor Typology)
dat_long <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(names(title_lookup))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = factor(Variable, levels = names(title_lookup))
  )

# 3a. Get max y per Variable x Typology
y_pos_df <- dat_long %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# 3b. Letters

  filter(Variable %in% names(title_lookup)) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = factor(Variable, levels = names(title_lookup))
  ) %>%
  left_join(y_pos_df, by = c("Variable", "Typology")) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max * 1.1
  )

# 4. Facet labels

# 5. Build plot (filled)

  ) +
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1. Colors by response variable
#-------------------------------------------------
response_colors <- c(
  "Total Zn (nM)"         = "slategray",
  "Free Zn (nM)"          = "darkslategray3",
  "Free Zn2+/Total (%)"   = "turquoise3",
  "Bioavailable Zn"       = "darkslategray" 
)

# Facet order
response_order <- c(
  "Total Zn (nM)",
  "Free Zn (nM)",
  "Free Zn2+/Total (%)",
  "Bioavailable Zn"
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2. Define letter nudges
#-------------------------------------------------
letter_nudge <- c(
  "Total Zn (nM)"                      = 1,
  "Free Zn (nM)"                       = 1,
  "Free Zn2+/Total (%)" = 0.05,
  "Bioavailable Zn"                    = 2
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 3. Map variable names -> response labels
#-------------------------------------------------
response_lookup <- c(
  "log_Zn_nM"         = "Total Zn (nM)",
  "log_Free_Zn_nM"    = "Free Zn (nM)", 
  "rel_prop_Zn"       = "Free Zn2+/Total (%)",
  "log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g" = "Bioavailable Zn"
)

vars_trace <- names(response_lookup)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 4. Long data
#-------------------------------------------------
dat_long_trace <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(vars_trace)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Typology,
    names_to  = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  mutate(
    Response = response_lookup[Variable],
    Response = factor(Response, levels = response_order)
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5a. Max y per Variable x Typology
#-------------------------------------------------
y_pos_df <- dat_long_trace %>%
  group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
  summarise(y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5b. Attach letters above groups
#-------------------------------------------------
letters_long_trace <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable %in% vars_trace) %>%
  mutate(
    Response = response_lookup[Variable],
    Response = factor(Response, levels = response_order)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    y_pos_df,
    by = c("Variable", "Typology")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max + letter_nudge[as.character(Response)]
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5c. Facet strip labels with a., b., c., d.
#-------------------------------------------------
facet_labs <- c(
  "Total Zn (nM)"                      = "a.~Total~Zn~(nM)",
  "Free Zn (nM)"                       = "b.~Free~Zn^{2*'+'}~(nM)",
  "Free Zn2+/Total (%)" = "d.~Free~Zn^{2*'+'}/Total~Zn~('%')",
  "Bioavailable Zn"                    = "c.~Bioavailable~Zn~(nmol~g^{-1}~wet)"
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 6. Plot
#-------------------------------------------------
bioavail_panel2 <- ggplot(
  dat_long_trace,
  aes(
    x     = Typology,
    y     = Value,
    color = Response,
    fill  = Response
  )
) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, size = 1, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    data = letters_long_trace,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = response_colors, breaks = response_order) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = response_colors, breaks = response_order) +
  facet_wrap(
  ~ Response,
  scales = "free_y",
  ncol = 2,
  labeller = labeller(
    Response = as_labeller(facet_labs, label_parsed)
  )
) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, angle = 30, hjust = 1, color = "black"),
    strip.text  = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.title  = element_text(size = 14)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Trace Elements by Stream Typology",
    x     = "Stream Typology",
    y     = expression(paste("Value [", log[10], "]"))
  )

bioavail_panel2

# Save
out_dir <- "Plots by typology"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Trace_elements_panel_Zn2.png"),

)
```

### e. All Zn Complexes

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 1. Define variables of interest (already linear nM)
#-------------------------------------------------
vars <- c(
  "Free_Zn_nM",
  "ZnOH_nM",
  "Zn_OH_2_nM",
  "ZnCO3_nM",
  "ZnHCO3_nM",
  "ZnSO4_nM",
  "ZnCl_nM",
  "ZnS_nM",
  "TOrg_Zn_nM"
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 2. Pivot to long format and summarize mean concentration
#    Bar height will now equal total mean Zn (nM)
#-------------------------------------------------
plot_dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(vars),
    names_to = "Species",
    values_to = "conc_nM"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Typology, Species) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_conc = mean(conc_nM, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 3. Clean legend labels
#-------------------------------------------------
plot_dat <- plot_dat %>%
  mutate(
    Species = Species %>%
      gsub("_nM", "", .) %>%
      gsub("_", " ", .),
    
    Species = dplyr::recode(Species,
      "Free Zn" = "Zn²⁺",
      "ZnOH" = "ZnOH",
      "Zn OH 2" = "Zn(OH)₂",
      "ZnCO3" = "ZnCO₃",
      "ZnHCO3" = "ZnHCO₃",
      "ZnSO4" = "ZnSO₄",
      "ZnCl" = "ZnCl",
      "ZnS" = "ZnS",
      "TOrg Zn" = "Organic-Zn"
    )
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 4. Order species by overall contribution
#-------------------------------------------------
plot_dat$Species <- factor(
  plot_dat$Species,
  levels = plot_dat %>%
    group_by(Species) %>%
    summarize(total = sum(mean_conc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(total)) %>%
    pull(Species)
)

species_levels <- levels(plot_dat$Species)

custom_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("brown", "yellow", "skyblue", "darkblue"))(
  length(species_levels)
)

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5. Plot stacked barplot
#    Total bar height = sum of species concentrations
#-------------------------------------------------
zn_species <- ggplot(plot_dat, aes(x = Typology, y = mean_conc, fill = Species)) +
  geom_col(color = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  labs(
    x = "Typology",
    y = "Total Zn (nM)",
    fill = "Zn Species",
    title = "Zinc Speciation by Typology"
  ) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )

zn_species

#-------------------------------------------------
# 6. Save
#-------------------------------------------------
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "All_Zn_Complexes.png"),
  plot     = zn_species,
  width    = 7,
  height   = 5,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

Table

```{r}
rel_table <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    total_zn_nM = rowSums(across(all_of(vars)), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  filter(total_zn_nM > 0) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(vars),
    names_to = "Species",
    values_to = "conc_nM"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    rel_conc = conc_nM / total_zn_nM
  ) %>%
  group_by(Typology, Species) %>%
  summarize(
    Mean   = mean(rel_conc, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    SD     = sd(rel_conc, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    Median = median(rel_conc, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Wide format (Mean %)
rel_table_wide <- rel_table %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, Species, Mean) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Species,
    values_from = Mean
  )

rel_table_wide

# 4. Save
library(openxlsx)

write.xlsx(
  rel_table_wide,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "Zn_species_relative_proportions.xlsx"),

)
```

```{r}
box_lookup <- c(
  "rel_prop_Zn"       = "b.~Free~Zn^{2*'+'}/Total~Zn~('%')",
  "log_TBL_Zn_nmol_g" = "c.~Bioavailable~Zn~(nmol~g^{-1}~wet)~'['~log[10]~']'"
)

box_colors <- c(
  "b.~Free~Zn^{2*'+'}/Total~Zn~('%')" = "darkgray",
  "c.~Bioavailable~Zn~(nmol~g^{-1}~wet)~'['~log[10]~']'" = "darkslategray"
)

box_dat <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(names(box_lookup))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Typology,
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Value)) %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = box_lookup[Variable],
    Panel = factor(
      Panel,
      levels = c(
  "a.~Zn~speciation~(nM)",
  "b.~Free~Zn^{2*'+'}/Total~Zn~('%')",
  "c.~Bioavailable~Zn~(nmol~g^{-1}~wet)~'['~log[10]~']'"
      )
    )
  )

species_dat <- species_dat %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = factor(
      Panel,
      levels = levels(box_dat$Panel)
    )
  )


#-------------------------------------------------
# 4. Letters for boxplot panels only
#-------------------------------------------------
letter_nudge <- c(
  "b.~Free~Zn^{2*'+'}/Total~Zn~('%')" = 0.05,
  "c.~Bioavailable~Zn~(nmol~g^{-1}~wet)~'['~log[10]~']'" = 0.7
)

letters_box <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable %in% names(box_lookup)) %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = box_lookup[Variable],
    Panel = factor(Panel, levels = levels(box_dat$Panel))
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    box_dat %>%
      group_by(Variable, Typology) %>%
      summarise(y_max = max(Value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
    by = c("Variable", "Typology")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max + letter_nudge[as.character(Panel)]
  )

letters_species <- letters_df %>%
  filter(Variable == "Zn_nM") %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = factor(
      "a.~Zn~speciation~(nM)",
      levels = levels(box_dat$Panel)
    )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    species_dat %>%
      group_by(Typology) %>%
      summarise(y_max = sum(mean_conc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "Typology"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y_pos = y_max * 1.3
  )


# Zn error bars
zn_error <- dat %>%
  group_by(Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_Zn = mean(Zn_nM, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_Zn   = sd(Zn_nM, na.rm = TRUE),
    n       = sum(!is.na(Zn_nM)),
    se_Zn   = sd_Zn / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    species_dat %>%
      group_by(Typology) %>%
      summarise(bar_height = sum(mean_conc, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "Typology"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Panel = factor("a.~Zn~speciation~(nM)", levels = levels(species_dat$Panel)),
    ymin = bar_height - se_Zn,
    ymax = bar_height + se_Zn
  )

#-------------------------------------------------
# 5. Combined faceted plot
#-------------------------------------------------
zn_combined_panel <- ggplot() +
  
  # Stacked mean species barplot
  geom_col(
    data = species_dat,
    aes(x = Typology, y = mean_conc, fill = Species),
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
  values = species_colors,
  name = "Zn species",
  guide = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
) +
  
  # Error bars for stacked barplot
  geom_errorbar(
  data = zn_error,
  aes(x = Typology, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
  inherit.aes = FALSE,
  width = 0.5,
  linewidth = 0.5,
  color = "black"
) +
  
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  
  # Boxplots
  geom_boxplot(
  data = box_dat,
  aes(x = Typology, y = Value, fill = Panel, color = Panel),
  width = 0.7,
  alpha = 0.4,   # slightly more transparent
  linewidth = 0.3
) +
geom_jitter(
  data = box_dat,
  aes(x = Typology, y = Value, color = Panel),
  width = 0.15,
  size = 0.7,    # slightly smaller points
  alpha = 0.7
)  +
  
  # Letters for Zn speciation stacked bars
  geom_text(
    data = letters_species,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  
  # Letters for boxplot panels
  geom_text(
    data = letters_box,
    aes(x = Typology, y = y_pos, label = Letters),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_manual(values = box_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = box_colors, guide = "none") +
  
    facet_wrap(
    ~ Panel,
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 3,
    labeller = labeller(Panel = label_parsed)
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Zinc Speciation and Bioavailability by Stream Typology",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Value"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
  legend.position = "bottom",
  legend.justification = "left",
  legend.background = element_blank(),
  legend.title = element_text(size = 9),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
  legend.box = "horizontal",
  axis.text.x = element_text(
    size = 10,
    angle = 30,
    hjust = 1,
    color = "black"
  ),
  axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
  strip.text = element_text(size = 12),
  plot.title = element_text(size = 14)
)

zn_combined_panel

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Zn_pub_plot.png"),
  plot     = zn_combined_panel,
  width    = 12,
  height   = 6,
  dpi      = 300
)
```

## 2. Overlap of measured vs toxic concentrations

Calculate probability of overlapping measured zinc with toxic levels of zinc by stream typology

```{r}
# Quantify overlapping area of measured zinc with chronic and acute toxic concentrations by typology

library(dplyr)
library(openxlsx)

# --- Define overlap function ---
overlap_area <- function(x, y, n = 512) {
  d1 <- density(x, na.rm = TRUE, n = n)
  d2 <- density(y, na.rm = TRUE, n = n)
  
  x_start <- max(min(d1$x), min(d2$x))
  x_end   <- min(max(d1$x), max(d2$x))
  
  if (x_start >= x_end) return(0)  # No overlap
  
  x_common <- seq(x_start, x_end, length.out = n)
  y1 <- approx(d1$x, d1$y, x_common)$y
  y2 <- approx(d2$x, d2$y, x_common)$y
  
  sum(pmin(y1, y2)) * diff(x_common[1:2])
}

# --- Compute overlaps by Typology ---
overlap_Zn_by_typology <- dat %>%
  group_by(Typology) %>%
  summarise(
    Overlap_Zn_Chronic = overlap_area(log_Zn_nM, log_Zn_chronic_tox_nM),
    Overlap_Zn_Acute   = overlap_area(log_Zn_nM, log_Zn_acute_tox_nM)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# View results
overlap_Zn_by_typology

# Save
library(openxlsx)
out_dir <- "Toxicity plots"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)

write.xlsx(
  overlap_Zn_by_typology,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "Zn_overlap_measured_vs_BLM_toxicity.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

## 3. MLE of Zn toxicity

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# Raw toxicity variables ----
vars <- c(
  "Zn_chronic_tox_nM",
  "Zn_acute_tox_nM"
)

mle_summary <- map_dfr(vars, function(var) {
  
  dat %>%
    dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(var)) %>%
    rename(value = all_of(var)) %>%
    
    filter(!is.na(Typology), !is.na(value)) %>%
    
    group_by(Typology) %>%
    summarise(
      variable = var,
      n = n(),
      mle_mean = mean(value),                         # μ̂
      mle_variance = mean((value - mean(value))^2),   # σ̂² (MLE, denominator = n)
      mle_sd = sqrt(mle_variance),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    
    dplyr::select(Typology, variable, n, mle_mean, mle_variance, mle_sd)
})

mle_summary

# Log10 toxicity variables ----
vars <- c(
  "log_Zn_chronic_tox_nM",
  "log_Zn_acute_tox_nM"
)

mle_summary_log <- map_dfr(vars, function(var) {

    dplyr::select(Typology, all_of(var)) %>%
    rename(value = all_of(var)) %>%
    
    filter(!is.na(Typology), !is.na(value)) %>%
    
    group_by(Typology) %>%
    summarise(
      variable = var,
      n = n(),
      mle_mean = mean(value),                         # μ̂
      mle_variance = mean((value - mean(value))^2),   # σ̂² (MLE, denominator = n)
      mle_sd = sqrt(mle_variance),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    
    dplyr::select(Typology, variable, n, mle_mean, mle_variance, mle_sd)
})
```

Determine the top predictors of chronic toxicity

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(car)
library(relaimpo)

#-------------------------------
# 1. Define candidate predictors
#-------------------------------
vars_to_select <- c(
  "log_Zn_nM", "log_Temp_C", 
  "pH", "log_DOC_nM", "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM", 
  "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM", 
  "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM"
)

#-------------------------------
# 2. Fit full model
#-------------------------------
full_formula <- as.formula(
  paste("log_Zn_chronic_tox_nM ~", paste(vars_to_select, collapse = " + "))
)

full_mod <- lm(full_formula, data = dat)

#-------------------------------
# 3. Stepwise model selection
#-------------------------------
step_mod <- step(full_mod, direction = "both", trace = TRUE)

#-------------------------------
# 4. Extract retained estimates
#-------------------------------
estimate_table <- broom::tidy(step_mod) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Variable = term,
    Estimate = estimate,
    Std_Error = std.error,
    p_value = p.value
  )

#-------------------------------
# 5. Extract VIF values
#-------------------------------
vif_table <- tibble(
  Variable = names(vif(step_mod)),
  VIF = as.numeric(vif(step_mod))
)

#-------------------------------
# 6. Calculate relative importance
#-------------------------------
rel_importance <- calc.relimp(step_mod, type = "lmg", rela = TRUE)

importance_table <- tibble(
  Variable = names(rel_importance$lmg),
  Relative_Importance = as.numeric(rel_importance$lmg)
)

#-------------------------------
# 7. Combine final table
#-------------------------------
final_model_table <- estimate_table %>%
  left_join(vif_table, by = "Variable") %>%
  left_join(importance_table, by = "Variable") %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(Estimate, Std_Error, p_value, VIF, Relative_Importance),
      ~ round(.x, 4)
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Relative_Importance))

final_model_table

#-------------------------------
# 8. Model fit statistics
#-------------------------------
model_summary <- summary(step_mod)

model_fit_table <- tibble(
  Metric = c("R_squared", "Adjusted_R_squared"),
  Value  = c(
    model_summary$r.squared,
    model_summary$adj.r.squared
  )
) %>%
  mutate(Value = round(Value, 4))

# Save
library(openxlsx)

file_path <- file.path(out_dir, "Chronic_Zn_toxicity_threshold_MLR.xlsx")

wb <- createWorkbook()

addWorksheet(wb, "Stepwise selected model")
writeData(wb, "Stepwise selected model", final_model_table)

addWorksheet(wb, "Model fit")
writeData(wb, "Model fit", model_fit_table)

saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
```

Stepwise MLR selection

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(car)
library(relaimpo)

#-------------------------------
# 1. Define candidate predictors
#-------------------------------
vars_to_select <- c(
  "log_Zn_nM", "log_Temp_C", 
  "pH", "log_DOC_nM", "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM", 
  "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM", 
  "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM"
)

#-------------------------------
# 2. Fit full model
#-------------------------------
full_formula <- as.formula(
  paste("log_Zn_acute_tox_nM ~", paste(vars_to_select, collapse = " + "))
)

full_mod <- lm(full_formula, data = dat)

#-------------------------------
# 3. Stepwise model selection
#-------------------------------
step_mod <- step(full_mod, direction = "both", trace = TRUE)

#-------------------------------
# 4. Extract retained estimates
#-------------------------------
estimate_table <- broom::tidy(step_mod) %>%
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Variable = term,
    Estimate = estimate,
    Std_Error = std.error,
    p_value = p.value
  )

#-------------------------------
# 5. Extract VIF values
#-------------------------------
vif_table <- tibble(
  Variable = names(vif(step_mod)),
  VIF = as.numeric(vif(step_mod))
)

#-------------------------------
# 6. Calculate relative importance
#-------------------------------
rel_importance <- calc.relimp(step_mod, type = "lmg", rela = TRUE)

importance_table <- tibble(
  Variable = names(rel_importance$lmg),
  Relative_Importance = as.numeric(rel_importance$lmg)
)

#-------------------------------
# 7. Combine final table
#-------------------------------
final_model_table <- estimate_table %>%
  left_join(vif_table, by = "Variable") %>%
  left_join(importance_table, by = "Variable") %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      c(Estimate, Std_Error, p_value, VIF, Relative_Importance),
      ~ round(.x, 4)
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Relative_Importance))

final_model_table

#-------------------------------
# 8. Model fit statistics
#-------------------------------
model_summary <- summary(step_mod)

model_fit_table <- tibble(
  Metric = c("R_squared", "Adjusted_R_squared"),
  Value  = c(
    model_summary$r.squared,
    model_summary$adj.r.squared
  )
) %>%
  mutate(Value = round(Value, 4))

# Save
library(openxlsx)

file_path <- file.path(out_dir, "Acute_Zn_toxicity_threshold_MLR.xlsx")

wb <- createWorkbook()

addWorksheet(wb, "Stepwise selected model")
writeData(wb, "Stepwise selected model", final_model_table)

addWorksheet(wb, "Model fit")
writeData(wb, "Model fit", model_fit_table)

saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
```

# Interaction effect of Typology and Developed LULC

Interaction effect for each BLM predictor \~ Typology \* Developed_lulc

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(broom)

vars <- c(
  "pH", "log_DOC_nM", "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM",
  "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM",
  "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM", "log_Zn_nM", "log_Cu_nM"
)

dat_long <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Typology, Developed_lulc, all_of(vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(vars),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

model_results <- dat_long %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(data, ~ lm(Value ~ Developed_lulc * Typology, data = .x)),
    tidy  = map(model, tidy)
  ) %>%
  unnest(tidy)

# Extract interaction terms
interaction_results <- model_results %>%
  filter(
    term == "(Intercept)" |
    term == "Developed_lulc" |
    grepl("Developed_lulc:Typology", term)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable, term, estimate, p.value) %>%
  mutate(
    significant = p.value < 0.05
  )

# Save
out_dir <- "Typology_Developed_lulc Interaction"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

library(openxlsx)

wb <- createWorkbook()

addWorksheet(wb, "Interaction_Results")

writeData(wb, "Interaction_Results", interaction_results)

saveWorkbook(
  wb,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "interaction_results.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

# Interaction of Typology and Time

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(broom)

vars <- c(
  "pH", "log_DOC_nM", "log_DIC_nM", "log_Cl_nM",
  "log_Ca_nM", "log_Mg_nM", "log_SO4_nM",
  "log_Na_nM", "log_K_nM", "log_Zn_nM", "log_Cu_nM"
)

dat_long <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(Date, Typology, all_of(vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(vars),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Date), !is.na(Value))

model_results <- dat_long %>%
  group_by(Variable) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    model = map(data, ~ lm(Value ~ Date * Typology, data = .x)),
    tidy  = map(model, tidy)
  ) %>%
  unnest(tidy)

# Extract interaction terms
interaction_results <- model_results %>%
  filter(
    term == "(Intercept)" |
    term == "Date" |
    grepl("Date:Typology", term)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Variable, term, estimate, p.value) %>%
  mutate(
    significant = p.value < 0.05
  )

# Save
out_dir <- "Typology_Date Interaction"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) {
  dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

library(openxlsx)

wb <- createWorkbook()

addWorksheet(wb, "Interaction_Results")

writeData(wb, "Interaction_Results", interaction_results)

saveWorkbook(
  wb,
  file = file.path(out_dir, "interaction_results.xlsx"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  
  labs(
    title = "Water Chemistry Over Time (Non-Perennial Tributaries)",
    x = "Date"
  )

# Save
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(out_dir, "Typology_date_nptribs.png"),
  plot     = a4,
  width    = 15,
  height   = 8,
  dpi      = 300
)
```
